content: Methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) are pH-dependent, meaning that the coadministration of antacids or acid suppressants may alter the release of methylphenidate. To avoid this interaction, consider separating the administration of antacids and methylphenidate extended-release capsules. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Do not exceed a mifepristone dose of 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as this combination may also prolong the QT interval. Consider alternative therapies if available. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. As mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, monitor for potential dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. Modafinil increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters, which raises momelotinib plasma concentrations and the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of inhaled mometasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulations are less sensitive to this interaction, but the clinical significance remains unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of nateglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may result in hypoglycemia. Monitor glucose levels closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of neomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is required. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may enhance the effects of calcium channel blockers, potentially leading to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may enhance the effects of calcium channel blockers, potentially leading to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Consider initiating nifedipine at the lowest dose available if coadministered with clarithromycin. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may enhance the effects of calcium channel blockers, potentially leading to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Do not exceed clarithromycin doses greater than 1,000 mg/day in patients taking protease inhibitors. Consider dose reduction in patients with renal impairment. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may enhance the effects of calcium channel blockers, potentially leading to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Clarithromycin and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir decrease the levels or effects of omeprazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor for decreased omeprazole efficacy and consider increasing the omeprazole dose in patients whose symptoms are not well controlled (not to exceed 40 mg/day). Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Both osilodrostat and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Osimertinib and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Oxcarbazepine increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ozanimod and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of pravastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for myopathy and do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when coadministered with clarithromycin.
